social_security.summary: Hawaii does not adopt the federal rule (IRC 86) that taxes Social Security and Tier 1 Railroad Retirement benefits, so they are not taxed.

public_pension.summary: Benefits from Hawaii's Employees' Retirement System and comparable benefits from other public retirement systems, and pensions for past services generally, are excluded from Hawaii income.
conditions: Amounts from voluntary employee contributions made under an elective right are not excluded (see notes)

sources.quote: (2) Rights, benefits, and other income exempted from taxation by section 88-91, having to do with the state retirement system, and the rights, benefits, and other income, comparable to the rights, benefits, and other income exempted by section 88-91, under any other public retirement system;
(3) Any compensation received in the form of a pension for past services; (4) Compensation paid to a patient affected with Hansen's disease

The legislature finds that there is a growing number of individuals moving to Hawaii to retire who may be receiving income through a pension for past services performed outside of the State. Currently, these pensions are not taxed under the state income tax law.

private_pension.summary: Employer-funded private pensions paid for past services are excluded from Hawaii income; distributions attributable to the employee's own contributions, such as 401(k) elective deferrals and IRAs, are taxable.
conditions: Employer-funded pension for past services: excluded
Portion from employee contributions (401(k) elective deferrals, IRAs): taxable (per DOTAX rules; see notes)

sources.quote: (3) Any compensation received in the form of a pension for past services; (4) Compensation paid to a patient affected with Hansen's disease

The legislature finds that there is a growing number of individuals moving to Hawaii to retire who may be receiving income through a pension for past services performed outside of the State. Currently, these pensions are not taxed under the state income tax law.

military_retirement.summary: U.S. military retired pay is a pension for past services and is not subject to Hawaii income tax.

sources.quote: (3) Any compensation received in the form of a pension for past services; (4) Compensation paid to a patient affected with Hansen's disease
Military retired pay is not subject to Hawaiʻi State income tax.

notes: The Department of Taxation states these rules mainly in its N-11/N-15 instructions and Tax Information Releases (e.g. TIR 96-5), all PDFs lexflow cannot read here, and no DOTAX web page stating them was found. Page sources are therefore other official State of Hawaii pages: the Legislature's text of 2024 HB1572 (a bill, not enacted, whose findings describe current law; the index text of 235-7(a)(3) is still unamended) and DBEDT's Hawaii Defense Economy page. social_security has a statute source only. The split for private plans (employer-funded portion excluded; amounts from employee contributions such as 401(k) elective deferrals and IRA distributions taxable) comes from DOTAX administrative rules (HAR 18-235-7-03) and form instructions, not from a quoted source, and should be confirmed. The 235-2.3 quote is an item in that section's list of Internal Revenue Code provisions that are not operative for Hawaii income tax.
